title: POC scoping - data handling & retention (Lifecare Health)
next_steps: SE to send POC architecture diagram and security whitepaper by 2026-05-12
AE to share pricing estimate and pilot terms by 2026-05-14
Customer to provide sample dataset and acceptance criteria by 2026-05-16
action_items: Priya Ghosh; run quick latency/cost estimate for 100 req/s, 512 tokens; due: 2026-05-12
Dana Rivera; share anonymized sample logs and PII profile; due: 2026-05-16
Evan Marshall; prep SOC2+ISO docs & KMS integration notes; due: 2026-05-12
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling requirements for a healthcare POC: what PII is present, redaction and logging controls, retention windows, prompt storage concerns, and benchmarks/trials. Agreement to provide sample data, run a bench at ~100 rps with 512-token avg, and validate redaction/retention via automated tests.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Evan Marshall (Redwood AE), Priya Ghosh (Redwood SE), Dana Rivera (Lifecare Head of Engineering), Marta Liu (Lifecare Security Director), Ahmed Khan (PM)

[00:00] Evan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros? we just wanna make sure we understand the data handling constraints for the POC.
[00:18] Dana: Hi, Dana here. We're running a small med imaging notes ingestion and chat triage flow. PII is present in the notes — names, dates, MRN, sometimes provider IDs.
[00:28] Marta: Marta, security. main asks are: no raw PII stored in logs, audit trail for any redaction, KMS for keys, and SOC2 evidence. Also retention windows enforceable per environment.
[00:40] Evan: Got it. Priya's the SE who'll scope the bench and the redaction flow. Priya, quick comment?
[00:45] Priya (SE): Sure, hi everyone. Couple things I wanna validate — do you expect Redwood-hosted API (hosted) for the POC, or Dedicated/Private? That affects log controls and where prompts are stored.
[01:00] Dana: We prefer Hosted for speed of onboarding, but if retention/logging constraints require, we can do Redwood Private behind our VPC. For POC speed though hosted would be ideal.
[01:12] Marta: Hosted is okay if we can guarantee prompt redaction and that raw prompts with PHI are never persisted beyond X hours and logs are redact-only. We also need proof that KV cache or prompt-cache doesn't leak PII across requests.
[01:27] Priya: Understood. On the runtime side we have options: hosted with strict retention settings and automatic redaction pre-ingest, or Private which gives you full control over storage. For hosted we can do request-side redaction hooks and a short retention policy, plus fake-anonymization before saving prompts.
[01:44] Ahmed: Can you describe what 'request-side redaction hooks' mean? do we control a pre-processing lambda or is it built into Redwood?
[01:52] Priya: It's flexible. For the POC, easiest is to run a small pre-processing step in your infra that strips or tokenizes PII before sending. Alternatively, Redwood can apply server-side redaction using regex/ML heuristics, but that means you send raw data to the hosted API briefly; we can configure no-persist flags and ephemeral processing.
[02:12] Marta: Ephemeral processing is a concern. We need to know about logging — access logs, application logs, debug traces. Who sees those? are they encrypted at rest and scoped to the org?
[02:22] Evan: All logs in hosted are encrypted at rest. For enterprise we can enable customer-managed KMS. Access is role-based; audit logs available in Console. For stricter needs, Private keeps everything in your VPC.
[02:35] Dana: What about prompts stored for evals or prompt-history? our team is worried prompts could be stored for model improvement or cache.
[02:44] Priya: We have an opt-in signal for model improvement; by default we'd mark POC traffic as no-training. For caching, runtime uses KV cache for attention keys — that's in-memory on the serving node and not persisted to long-term storage. We can also disable KV persistence and ensure caches are flushed per session.
[03:05] Marta: Is KV cache persisted to disk under high load? we've seen vendors spin to-disk caches when memory pressure occurs.
[03:12] Priya: Good callout. For the POC config we'll pin instance types and policies so we don't spill to disk. We can also request that kernel dumps and swap are disabled and provide controls to prevent spill. Will add that to action items.
[03:28] Ahmed: Sizing — we're thinking 100 concurrent active chats during peak; average payload ~512 tokens input, 256 tokens output. Is that realistic?
[03:37] Priya: For 100 rps peak (or 100 concurrent?) — can you clarify?
[03:41] Ahmed: Sorry, 100 requests per second during peak for the triage endpoint.
[03:45] Priya: That's a helpful number. For 100 req/s at 512 tokens, latency SLOs will depend on model choice and batching. For hosted we can propose a 3x plan: baseline with open 7B quantized, mid with 13B, and high with a tuned 33B; benchmarks we'll run to show latency vs cost.
[04:07] Dana: Our success criteria for POC: 95th percentile latency <800ms for common flows, no persisted PII, and less than X cost per 1k tokens — we'll define X after we see numbers. Also quality thresholds on accuracy of redaction and hallucination rate <3% on a set of test prompts.
[04:25] Evan: Perfect, that's actionable. We'll scope a benchmark with the three model tiers. Priya will run internal bench and then replicate on your sample data.
[04:35] Marta: Another thing: retention windows. For production we need prompts retained 0-24h in logs, and all prompts/outputs older than 30 days must be purgeable on demand. For POC we can tolerate shorter windows but we need API-driven purge endpoints and proof of deletion.
[04:52] Priya: Redwood hosted supports configurable log retention; we can set it to 24 hours for the POC, and we have an API to delete logs immediately for specific request IDs. We'll include a deletion audit entry showing who/when.
[05:05] Ahmed: For the PII redaction, can Redwood provide sample redaction rules? we'd like to maintain our own rule set; regex plus NER would be our preference.
[05:14] Priya: Yes — we can ship a starter set of regexes and an ML-based NER you can tune. We'll run a redaction pass and provide a report of redaction precision/recall against your sample set.
[05:26] Dana: On prompts stored for debugging, we want a way to mask patient names but keep context, e.g., replace names with consistent placeholders so threads remain coherent.
[05:35] Priya: We support deterministic tokenization/placeholder substitution so the same patient maps to the same pseudonym in a session. That can be enabled in the redaction pipeline.
[05:45] Marta: Audit logging: need immutability, must show original request ID, redaction version used, and operator who viewed any unredacted content. Also SSO + RBAC enforced for Console access.
[05:57] Evan: We can enable SAML SSO and map roles. Audit logs are append-only and we can provide export in NDJSON for your SIEM. For immutability we can provide signed log entries if needed.
[06:12] Ahmed: Anything else around encryption? we use AES-256 everywhere and HSM for key rotation.
[06:18] Priya: Redwood supports CMEK via your cloud KMS or on-prem HSM in Private. Keys rotate per your policy; we can show the KMS integration steps in the security doc.
[06:30] Dana: Good. Let's talk about acceptance test for redaction: we'll provide 500 labeled examples with PII. Success is >= 98% redaction coverage and <1% false positive on sensitive clinical terms. Is that ok?
[06:44] Priya: That's a clear metric. We'll run the redaction pipeline and return a detailed report. We'll also include a manual spot-check.
[06:52] Evan: Bench methodology: Priya will run three staged tests: synthetic load at target TPS with non-PII payloads to get baseline latency/cost, then run on anonymized real samples to test redaction and quality, then run with redaction disabled to measure raw performance.
[07:08] Marta: For the audit during POC, we want tiktok of who viewed unredacted content; is there a simple flag to log access to unredacted payloads?
[07:17] Priya: Yes, access to raw is gated and logged. We can also require Just-In-Time (JIT) access for unredacted content — operator has to request time-limited authorization.
[07:27] Ahmed: Timeline — we're aiming to start the POC the week of 2026-05-19 and run for 3 weeks. Benchmarks and initial redaction report in week 1, integration in week 2, acceptance tests in week 3.
[07:39] Evan: That timeline is feasible. We'll need sample data and a point of contact for data transfer.
[07:45] Dana: I'll get IT to prepare a sanitized dataset — needs to be representative with edge cases. We'll also provide acceptance criteria doc.
[07:53] Priya: For the benchmark run we'll need a small harness — we can share a JMeter/postman collection or a simple python runner. Which do you prefer?
[08:01] Ahmed: Python runner is fine. We want something reproducible in our CI.
[08:06] Priya: Cool, we'll share that.
[08:09] Marta: One other question — do you preserve prompts for model debug internally for a limited time, even with no-training? sometimes vendors sandbox logs for 72 hours for debugging.
[08:18] Evan: For hosted no-training traffic, we still retain ephemeral debug logs for up to 24 hours for operational telemetry and then purge; we can reduce to 6 hours for the POC if you require.
[08:28] Marta: We'd prefer 6 hours and immediate purge on request.
[08:31] Priya: Noted. We'll set 6 hours default and provide the delete API for request-specific purge.
[08:37] Dana: Are there any limitations around HIPAA? we need BAAs for production. For POC we can do a limited data set but still want to ensure controls.
[08:45] Evan: We do BAA for Dedicated/Private; for hosted POC we can sign a BAA under specific terms — I'll flag legal. For production Dedicated or Private is typical.
[08:55] Ahmed: Any known gotchas around latency when enabling redaction pipeline?
[09:00] Priya: Inline redaction adds a small pre-processing cost — typically 20-60ms depending on complexity. If latency is critical we can do client-side redaction to avoid the server step. We'll measure in bench.
[09:12] Marta: For retention rules, can we tag requests by sensitivity level and enforce different windows?
[09:17] Priya: Yes, we support metadata tags on requests and policy engine to map to retention TTLs. We'll demo that in the Console.
[09:26] Evan: OK, quick recap and next steps: Priya sends architecture and bench plan by Tue (2026-05-12), Evan sends security docs and BAA flag to legal by Thu (2026-05-14), Lifecare to provide sample dataset and acceptance criteria by 2026-05-16, schedule bench week of 2026-05-19.
[09:47] Dana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:50] Evan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with links to the redaction rules doc, the runner repo, and the POC checklist.
[10:00] End of meeting
